title: श्रीमद्भगवद्गीता — श्रद्धात्रयविभागयोगः
titleEn: The Bhagavad Gītā — Chapter 17: The Three Kinds of Faith
draftNote: Prepared by the Lectorium pipeline from the vulgate text, with a drafting pass, a reviewing pass and a mechanical gate; a printed-edition collation and audio are still to come. Use ⚑ correction on any verse to report a problem.
source: Text: the received (vulgate) text of the Bhagavadgītā, Mahābhārata 6.23–40, as read by Śaṅkara's commentary. Devanagari from Sanskrit Wikisource (भगवद्गीता/श्रद्धात्रयविभागयोगः), collated verse by verse against the GRETIL romanized text based on the BORI critical edition (input Tokunaga, rev. J. Smith); every verse where the two differ carries a note giving the BORI reading, and every correction to the Wikisource text is named in its note. Collation against a pre-1930 printed edition is still to be done. Transliteration: IAST. The reading under each word gives the words with sandhi undone and compound members hyphenated, in the manner of the traditional pada-pāṭha. Pronunciation convention: classical Sanskrit as described in Whitney's Sanskrit Grammar (1889); no audio yet. Translations made fresh from the Sanskrit with Monier-Williams (1899), Apte (1890) and Śaṅkara's commentary for the traditional sense; no modern translation consulted.

sentences.t: अर्जुन उवाच
sentences.tr: arjuna uvāca
sentences.l: Arjuna said

morph.gloss: Arjuna, the third Pāṇḍava, the great archer (nom. sg.)
to speak (uvāca: perfect 3rd sg. 'said')

sentences.t:
ये शास्त्रविधिमुत्सृज्य यजन्ते श्रद्धयान्विताः ।
तेषां निष्ठा तु का कृष्ण सत्त्वमाहो रजस्तमः ॥
sentences.tr:
ye śāstra-vidhim utsṛjya yajante śraddhayā anvitāḥ |
teṣām niṣṭhā tu kā kṛṣṇa sattvam āho rajaḥ tamaḥ ||

morph.gloss: who, which (ye: nom. pl. masc. relative)
scripture, sacred teaching (first member)
injunction, rule (śāstra-vidhim: 'the injunction of scripture', acc. sg. masc., object of utsṛjya; simply joined with utsṛjya)
to abandon, cast aside (utsṛjya: gerund, 'having abandoned')
to sacrifice (yajante: present middle 3rd pl., 'they sacrifice')
faith (instr. sg. 'with faith')
endowed with, possessed of (past participle of anu-i; anvitāḥ: nom. pl. masc., agreeing with the implied subject 'those who'; śraddhayā+anvitāḥ→śraddhayānvitāḥ, ā+a→ā)
they (teṣām: gen. pl. 'of them')
steadfastness, standing, fixed state (nom. sg. fem., subject)
but, now (particle)
what? (kā: nom. sg. fem. interrogative)
Kṛṣṇa (vocative)
sattva, kept untranslated, one of the three guṇas (nom. sg. neut.)
or (interrogative disjunctive particle; sattvam+āho simply joined, final -m unaffected before the vowel)
rajas, kept untranslated (nom. sg. neut.; -aḥ+t-→-as t-)
tamas, kept untranslated (nom. sg. neut.)

sentences.l: Who, the injunction-of-scripture having-abandoned, sacrifice endowed-with-faith — of them the steadfastness, but, what, Kṛṣṇa? Sattva, or rajas, tamas?
sentences.i: Those who, disregarding the injunction of scripture, offer sacrifice endowed with faith — what is their footing, Kṛṣṇa? Is it sattva, or rajas, or tamas?
sentences.n: Arjuna opens the chapter with a question left over from the last: chapter 16 closed by making scripture (śāstra) the standard for action, and here Arjuna asks about people who ignore that standard yet still sacrifice with real fervor (śraddhayā anvitāḥ, 'endowed with faith' — śraddhayā+anvitāḥ, ā+a→ā). Niṣṭhā, 'steadfastness, footing, standing', asks what ground such people are really standing on. Sattvam āho rajas tamaḥ is not a compound: sattva, rajas and tamas are three separate alternatives (rajaḥ tamaḥ simply written together at their sandhi boundary, -aḥ+t-→-as t-), with āho, 'or', an interrogative disjunctive particle. This opens the chapter's governing question — is faith itself always good, or does its worth depend on which guṇa shapes it? — which Kṛṣṇa begins to answer immediately in verse 2. Sattva, rajas, tamas, the three guṇas, are kept untranslated throughout, per convention.

sentences.t: श्रीभगवानुवाच
sentences.tr: śrībhagavān uvāca
sentences.l: The Blessed Lord said

morph.gloss: holy, glorious (honorific prefix)

sentences.t:
त्रिविधा भवति श्रद्धा देहिनां सा स्वभावजा ।
सात्त्विकी राजसी चैव तामसी चेति तां शृणु ॥
sentences.tr:
trividhā bhavati śraddhā dehinām sā svabhāvajā |
sāttvikī rājasī ca eva tāmasī ca iti tām śṛṇu ||

morph.gloss: threefold (trividhā: nom. sg. fem., agreeing with śraddhā)
to be, become (bhavati: present 3rd sg.)
faith (nom. sg. fem., subject)
the embodied [being] (dehinām: gen. pl., 'of embodied beings')
she, it (sā: nom. sg. fem., resuming śraddhā)
born of one's own nature (nom. sg. fem., predicate)
sattva-natured, belonging to sattva (sāttvikī: nom. sg. fem.; sattva kept untranslated per convention)
rajas-natured, belonging to rajas (nom. sg. fem.; rajas kept untranslated)
and
indeed (ca+eva→caiva, a+e→ai)
tamas-natured, belonging to tamas (nom. sg. fem.; tamas kept untranslated)
and (ca+iti→ceti, a+i→e)
thus (closing the enumeration)
that, it (tām: acc. sg. fem., object of śṛṇu, referring to śraddhā)
to hear (śṛṇu: imperative 2nd sg., 'hear!')

sentences.l: Threefold comes-to-be the-faith of-embodied-beings, it, born-of-own-nature: sattva-natured, and rajas-natured, and-indeed tamas-natured — thus; hear it.
sentences.i: The faith of embodied beings is of three kinds, born of their own nature: sattva-natured, rajas-natured, and tamas-natured. Hear now what these are.
sentences.n: Kṛṣṇa answers directly, with no speaker-line question of his own (the speaker line at the head of this verse is generated separately; see conventions.md). Svabhāvajā, 'born of one's own nature', makes the chapter's first and most important claim: faith is not simply chosen, it grows out of the disposition each person already has. Sāttvikī, rājasī, tāmasī are feminine forms agreeing with śraddhā; ca eva fuses to caiva (a+e→ai) and ca iti to ceti (a+i→e). This threefold division of faith itself, before any of its outward expressions, frames everything that follows through verse 22.

sentences.t:
सत्त्वानुरूपा सर्वस्य श्रद्धा भवति भारत ।
श्रद्धामयोऽयं पुरुषो यो यच्छ्रद्धः स एव सः ॥
sentences.tr:
sattva-anurūpā sarvasya śraddhā bhavati bhārata |
śraddhā-mayaḥ ayam puruṣaḥ yaḥ yat-śraddhaḥ sa eva saḥ ||

morph.gloss: one's own being, disposition (here the individual's inner nature or constitution, not the guṇa named in its narrower sense — see note; first member)
conforming to, corresponding to (sattva-anurūpā: 'conformed to one's own nature', nom. sg. fem., predicate; a+a→ā)
every, all (sarvasya: gen. sg. 'of everyone, of each')
faith (nom. sg. fem., subject)
to be, become (bhavati: present 3rd sg.)
descendant of Bharata, Arjuna (vocative)
faith (first member)
made of, consisting of (śraddhā-mayaḥ: 'made of faith', nom. sg. masc., predicate; -aḥ+a-→-o' with avagraha)
this (ayam: nom. sg. masc., subject)
a person, a man (nom. sg. masc., subject; -aḥ before y-→-o)
who (yaḥ: nom. sg. masc. relative; -aḥ before y-→-o)
what, whatever (first member; -t+ś-→-c ch-)
having ... faith (bahuvrīhi compound member; yat-śraddhaḥ: 'he whose faith is what [it is]', nom. sg. masc.)
he (sa: nom. sg. masc.; the pronoun sa/eṣa always drops its visarga before a following consonant)
indeed, precisely
he (saḥ: nom. sg. masc., repeated for emphasis, 'he is precisely that')

sentences.l: Conformed-to-[one's-own]-nature of-everyone, faith comes-to-be, Bhārata; made-of-faith [is] this person: who has-whatever-faith, he indeed [is] that.
sentences.i: Each person's faith conforms to his own nature, Bhārata. A person is made of faith: whatever his faith is, that indeed is what he is.
sentences.n: Sattva-anurūpā is ambiguous and worth flagging: here sattva does not mean the guṇa named in verse 1, but (per Śaṅkara) the antaḥkaraṇa, one's inner constitution or disposition — the particular blend of the three guṇas peculiar to each person — so it is translated 'nature' rather than left as the untranslated guṇa-name. Yat-śraddhaḥ (yad+śraddha, -t+ś-→-c ch-) is a bahuvrīhi, 'he whose faith is such-and-such'; sa eva saḥ doubles the pronoun for emphasis, 'he is precisely that' — the poem's most compact statement that a person's character is his faith. The pronoun sa (not saḥ) is written without visarga before any consonant, a standing exception in Sanskrit orthography.

sentences.t:
यजन्ते सात्त्विका देवान्यक्षरक्षांसि राजसाः ।
प्रेतान्भूतगणांश्चान्ये यजन्ते तामसा जनाः ॥
sentences.tr:
yajante sāttvikāḥ devān yakṣa-rakṣāṃsi rājasāḥ |
pretān bhūta-gaṇān ca anye yajante tāmasāḥ janāḥ ||

morph.gloss: to sacrifice (yajante: present middle 3rd pl.)
sattva-natured, belonging to sattva (nom. pl. masc.; -āḥ before d-→-ā)
god (devān: acc. pl., object of yajante in the first clause)
a yakṣa, a class of demigod, a nature-spirit (first member)
a rākṣasa, a class of demon (yakṣa-rakṣāṃsi: 'yakṣas and rākṣasas', acc. pl. neut. dvandva, object of yajante understood in the second clause)
rajas-natured, belonging to rajas (nom. pl. masc., subject)
a departed spirit, a ghost (pretān: acc. pl., object of yajante)
a host of bhūtas, spirits, elemental beings (bhūtagaṇān: acc. pl.; -n+c-→-ṃś c-)
and
other (anye: nom. pl. masc., agreeing with janāḥ; ca+anye→cānye, a+a→ā)
to sacrifice (yajante: present middle 3rd pl.)
tamas-natured, belonging to tamas (nom. pl. masc.; -āḥ before j-→-ā)
a person, people (nom. pl. masc., subject)

sentences.l: The-sattva-natured sacrifice to-gods; to-yakṣas-and-rākṣasas, the-rajas-natured; and to-ghosts-and-hosts-of-spirits, other tamas-natured people sacrifice.
sentences.i: The sattva-natured worship the gods; the rajas-natured worship yakṣas and rākṣasas; and other, tamas-natured people worship ghosts and hosts of spirits.
sentences.n: Verse 2's threefold faith is now shown in its first outward form — the object of worship each type of person is drawn to. Yakṣa-rakṣāṃsi is a dvandva (pair-compound), 'yakṣas and rākṣasas', taking the neuter plural ending of its last member rakṣas; yakṣas and rākṣasas, like preta ('a departed spirit, a ghost') and bhūta-gaṇa ('a host of elemental spirits'), are kept as their proper Sanskrit class-names rather than translated, following the pipeline's practice for such mythological categories (cf. 10.23, 11.22). Anye, 'other', agrees with tāmasāḥ janāḥ, completing the triad of worshippers that matches verse 2's triad of faith.

sentences.t:
अशास्त्रविहितं घोरं तप्यन्ते ये तपो जनाः ।
दम्भाहंकारसंयुक्ताः कामरागबलान्विताः ॥
sentences.tr:
a-śāstra-vihitam ghoram tapyante ye tapaḥ janāḥ |
dambha-ahaṃkāra-saṃyuktāḥ kāma-rāga-bala-anvitāḥ ||

morph.gloss: not [enjoined by] scripture (first member)
enjoined, ordained (past participle of vi-dhā; a-śāstra-vihitam: 'not enjoined by scripture', acc. sg. neut., agreeing with tapaḥ)
terrible, dreadful (acc. sg. neut.)
to practice austerity, to torment oneself (tapyante: present middle 3rd pl.)
who (ye: nom. pl. masc. relative)
austerity (acc. sg. neut., object of tapyante, 'practice austerity'; -aḥ before j-→-o)
a person, people (nom. pl. masc., subject)
hypocrisy, ostentation (first member)
egotism, the sense of 'I' (second member)
joined with, endowed with (past participle of sam-yuj; dambha-ahaṃkāra-saṃyuktāḥ: 'joined with hypocrisy and egotism', nom. pl. masc., predicate)
desire (first member)
passion, attachment (second member)
force, power (third member; bala+anvitāḥ→balānvitāḥ, a+a→ā)
possessed by, filled with (kāma-rāga-bala-anvitāḥ: 'possessed by the force of desire and passion', nom. pl. masc., predicate)

sentences.l: Terrible austerity-not-enjoined-by-scripture practice the-people who [do so], joined-with-hypocrisy-and-egotism, possessed-by-the-force-of-desire-and-passion,
sentences.i: Those people who practice terrible austerities not enjoined by scripture, joined with hypocrisy and egotism, driven by the force of desire and passion,
sentences.n: This verse opens a sentence that the main verb (viddhi, 'know') completes only in verse 6 — a relative-correlative spanning both verses (ye ... tān). A-śāstra-vihitam, 'not enjoined by scripture', recalls the very standard chapter 16 closed on (śāstraṃ pramāṇaṃ te, 16.24) and that verse 1's question already invoked; dambha, 'hypocrisy', was named repeatedly among the demonic traits of chapter 16 (16.4, 17-18). Tapaḥ here is the accusative object of tapyante ('they practice austerity'), not yet the topic named formally at verse 7.

sentences.t:
कर्षयन्तः शरीरस्थं भूतग्राममचेतसः ।
मां चैवान्तःशरीरस्थं तान्विद्ध्यासुरनिश्चयान् ॥
sentences.tr:
karṣayantaḥ śarīra-stham bhūta-grāmam acetasaḥ |
mām ca eva antar-śarīra-stham tān viddhi āsura-niścayān ||

morph.gloss: to drag, torment, afflict (karṣayant-: causative present participle, 'tormenting, dragging down'; karṣayantaḥ: nom. pl. masc. — the vulgate reading, printed here; the BORI critical edition reads karśayantaḥ, from kṛś 'to make thin, emaciate, waste away' — 'emaciating' — in its place: a real vulgate/BORI variant, not a misprint; see the note)
body (first member)
situated in, abiding in (śarīra-stham: 'situated in the body', acc. sg. masc., agreeing with bhūta-grāmam)
element, being (first member)
aggregate, multitude, host (bhūta-grāmam: 'the aggregate of [bodily] elements', acc. sg. masc., object of karṣayantaḥ)

mindless, without understanding (acetasaḥ: nom. pl. masc., agreeing with the subject 'they', carried over from verse 5's janāḥ; bhūtagrāmam+acetasaḥ simply joined, final -m unaffected before the vowel)
I (mām: acc. sg., object of viddhi, 'me too')
and
indeed, too (ca+eva→caiva, a+e→ai; caiva+antar-→caivāntar-, a+a→ā)
within, inside (surface form antaḥ- before the unvoiced ś-; first member)
body (second member)
situated in, dwelling in (antar-śarīra-stham: 'dwelling within the body', acc. sg. masc., agreeing with mām)
those (tān: acc. pl., referring back to verse 5's ye janāḥ, 'those people')
to know (viddhi: imperative 2nd sg., 'know!'; viddhi+āsura-→viddhyāsura-, -i+ā-→-y ā-)
demonic (first member)
resolve, determination, conviction (āsura-niścayān: 'of demonic resolve', acc. pl. masc., predicate complement of tān)

sentences.l: Tormenting the-aggregate-of-[bodily]-elements situated-in-the-body, mindless, and me too, dwelling-within-the-body — know them [to be] of-demonic-resolve.
sentences.i: Mindlessly they torment the mass of elements that make up the body, and me as well, dwelling within it — know them to be demonic in their resolve.
sentences.n: This is the chapter's one point where the received (vulgate) text, printed here, differs from the BORI critical edition: the vulgate reads karṣayantaḥ, 'tormenting, dragging down' (from √kṛṣ), where BORI reads karśayantaḥ, 'emaciating, wasting away' (from √kṛś) — a real vulgate/BORI variant, not a misprint. Bhūta-grāmam, 'the aggregate of [bodily] elements', names the physical body itself, contrasted with antar-śarīra-stham mām, 'me, dwelling within the body' (surface antaḥ- before the unvoiced ś-) — the same inner presence taught elsewhere as the kṣetrajña (ch. 13) or the self seated in the heart (15.15). Tān, 'those', picks up verse 5's ye, closing the two-verse sentence; āsura-niścayān, 'of demonic resolve', is Kṛṣṇa's verdict on such self-torturers, who harm not only their own bodies but, unknowingly, the god within them.

sentences.t:
आहारस्त्वपि सर्वस्य त्रिविधो भवति प्रियः ।
यज्ञस्तपस्तथा दानं तेषां भेदमिमं शृणु ॥
sentences.tr:
āhāraḥ tu api sarvasya trividhaḥ bhavati priyaḥ |
yajñaḥ tapaḥ tathā dānam teṣām bhedam imam śṛṇu ||

morph.gloss: food (āhāraḥ: nom. sg. masc., subject; -aḥ+t-→-as t-)
but, now (particle; tu+api→tvapi, -u+a-→-v a-, yaṇ sandhi)
also, indeed
everyone, all (sarvasya: gen. sg. 'of everyone')
threefold (trividhaḥ: nom. sg. masc., predicate; -aḥ before bh-→-o)
to be, become (bhavati: present 3rd sg.)
dear, pleasing (nom. sg. masc., predicate)
sacrifice (yajñaḥ: nom. sg. masc.; -aḥ+t-→-as t-)

giving (nom. sg. neut.)
they (teṣām: gen. pl. 'of these [three]')

this (imam: acc. sg. masc.)
to hear (śṛṇu: imperative 2nd sg.)

sentences.l: Food too, indeed, of-everyone threefold comes-to-be, dear; sacrifice, austerity, and-likewise giving — of-these this distinction, hear.
sentences.i: Food too is dear to everyone, but of three different kinds; so are sacrifice, austerity, and giving. Hear now how they differ.
sentences.n: This verse names the chapter's remaining four topics — āhāra ('food', vv. 8-10), yajña ('sacrifice', vv. 11-13), tapas ('austerity', vv. 14-19) and dāna ('giving', vv. 20-22) — each to be classified, like faith and worship before them, into its sattva-, rajas- and tamas-natured forms. Priyaḥ, 'dear, agreeable', signals that what a person finds appetizing or satisfying is itself diagnostic of guṇa, just as what they worship was in verse 4.

sentences.t:
आयुःसत्त्वबलारोग्यसुखप्रीतिविवर्धनाः ।
रस्याः स्निग्धाः स्थिरा हृद्या आहाराः सात्त्विकप्रियाः ॥
sentences.tr:
āyuḥ-sattva-bala-ārogya-sukha-prīti-vivardhanāḥ |
rasyāḥ snigdhāḥ sthirāḥ hṛdyāḥ āhārāḥ sāttvika-priyāḥ ||

morph.gloss: lifespan, length of life (first member)
vitality, vigor, strength of mind (here a secondary sense of the word, not the guṇa named as such — see note; second member)
strength (third member; bala+ārogya→balārogya, a+ā→ā)
health, freedom from illness (fourth member)
happiness (fifth member)
satisfaction, pleasure (sixth member)
increasing, promoting (āyuḥ-sattva-bala-ārogya-sukha-prīti-vivardhanāḥ: 'increasing lifespan, vitality, strength, health, happiness and satisfaction', nom. pl. masc., predicate agreeing with āhārāḥ)
savory, juicy, full of flavor (nom. pl. masc.)
unctuous, smooth, rich (nom. pl. masc.)
firm, substantial, lasting (nom. pl. masc.; -āḥ before h-→-ā)
agreeable to the heart, pleasing (nom. pl. masc.; -āḥ before ā-→-ā)
food (nom. pl. masc., subject)
sattva-natured, belonging to sattva (first member)
dear to (sāttvika-priyāḥ: 'dear to the sattva-natured', nom. pl. masc., predicate)

sentences.l: Lifespan-vitality-strength-health-happiness-and-satisfaction-increasing; savory, unctuous, firm, heart-pleasing — [such] foods [are] dear-to-the-sattva-natured.
sentences.i: Foods that increase lifespan, vitality, strength, health, happiness, and satisfaction; savory, rich, substantial, and pleasing to the heart — such foods are dear to the sattva-natured.
sentences.n: This opens the food-triad (vv. 8-10). The long opening compound āyuḥ-sattva-bala-ārogya-sukha-prīti-vivardhanāḥ packs six benefits into one word; note that sattva here means 'vitality, vigor' — a secondary sense of the word distinct from its use as one of the three guṇas named throughout this chapter (compare the different, generic sense of sattva already flagged at verse 3). Rasyāḥ, snigdhāḥ, sthirāḥ, hṛdyāḥ describe food by taste and texture rather than nutritional effect, closing with sāttvika-priyāḥ, 'dear to the sattva-natured', the formula this triad repeats for each guṇa (cf. verses 9-10).

grief (second member; śoka+āmaya→śokāmaya, a+ā→ā)
disease, sickness (third member)
causing, bestowing (duḥkha-śoka-āmaya-pradāḥ: 'causing pain, grief and disease', nom. pl. masc., predicate)

sentences.l: Pungent-sour-salty-excessively-hot-sharp-dry-burning — [such] foods [are] favored-of-the-rajas-natured, causing-pain-grief-and-disease.
sentences.i: Foods that are pungent, sour, salty, very hot, acrid, dry, and burning — these are favored by the rajas-natured, and they bring on pain, grief, and disease.
sentences.n: The rajas-natured diet, named through a seven-member compound whose internal sandhi is worth tracing: kaṭu+amla→kaṭvamla (u+a→va, yaṇ), lavaṇa+ati→lavaṇāti (a+a→ā), ati+uṣṇa→atyuṣṇa (i+u→yu, yaṇ). Duḥkha-śoka-āmaya-pradāḥ, 'causing pain, grief and disease', states the cost of such food as bluntly as verse 8 stated sattva's food's benefits.

sentences.t:
यातयामं गतरसं पूति पर्युषितं च यत् ।
उच्छिष्टमपि चामेध्यं भोजनं तामसप्रियम् ॥
sentences.tr:
yāta-yāmam gata-rasam pūti paryuṣitam ca yat |
ucchiṣṭam api ca amedhyam bhojanam tāmasa-priyam ||

morph.gloss: gone, passed (first member)
a watch, a period of time (yāta-yāmam: 'past its [proper] time, stale', nom. sg. neut., agreeing with bhojanam)
gone (first member)
flavor, savour, juice (gata-rasam: 'having lost its flavor, flat', nom. sg. neut.)
putrid, stinking (uninflected stem form, used adjectivally, agreeing with bhojanam)
kept overnight, spoiled with age (paryuṣita: past participle; nom. sg. neut.)
and
that which (yat: nom. sg. neut. relative, resuming as bhojanam, closing the description)
a remnant of a meal, food left over, ritually impure (ucchiṣṭam: nom. sg. neut.; simply joined with api, final -m unaffected before the vowel)
also, even
and (ca+amedhyam→cāmedhyam, a+a→ā)
impure, unfit for sacrifice (amedhyam: nom. sg. neut.)
food (nom. sg. neut., subject)
tamas-natured, belonging to tamas (first member)
dear to (tāmasa-priyam: 'dear to the tamas-natured', nom. sg. neut., predicate)

sentences.l: Stale, flat, putrid, and kept-overnight, and also — leftover and impure — food [is] dear-to-the-tamas-natured.
sentences.i: Food that is stale, flat, putrid, and kept overnight, and also food that is leftover and unclean — such food is dear to the tamas-natured.
sentences.n: Closes the food-triad. Yāta-yāmam, literally 'past its watch', is the standard idiom for stale food; gata-rasam, 'having lost its flavor'; ucchiṣṭam, 'a remnant of a meal', and amedhyam, 'unfit for sacrifice, impure', name food considered ritually unclean as well as physically unappetizing. Bhojana, 'food', here simply varies āhāra of verses 8-9.

sentences.t:
अफलाकाङ्क्षिभिर्यज्ञो विधिदृष्टो य इज्यते ।
यष्टव्यमेवेति मनः समाधाय स सात्त्विकः ॥
sentences.tr:
a-phala-ākāṅkṣibhiḥ yajñaḥ vidhi-dṛṣṭaḥ yaḥ ijyate |
yaṣṭavyam eva iti manaḥ samādhāya sa sāttvikaḥ ||

morph.gloss: fruitless, without [regard for] the fruit (first member; a-phala+ākāṅkṣibhiḥ→aphalākāṅkṣibhiḥ, a+ā→ā)
desiring, wishing for (a-phala-ākāṅkṣibhiḥ: 'by those not desiring the fruit', instr. pl. masc.; ākāṅkṣibhiḥ+yajñaḥ→ākāṅkṣibhiryajñaḥ, -iḥ+y-→-ir y-)
sacrifice (yajñaḥ: nom. sg. masc., subject; -aḥ before v-→-o)
injunction, rule (first member)
seen, hence prescribed (past participle of dṛś; vidhi-dṛṣṭaḥ: 'as prescribed by rule', nom. sg. masc., predicate; -aḥ before y-→-o)
which (yaḥ: nom. sg. masc. relative; visarga elided before the following vowel i-, hiatus retained — an accepted epic-verse option, already noted at 16.1's svādhyāyas tapa ārjavam)
to sacrifice (ijyate: present passive 3rd sg., 'is offered')
to sacrifice (yaṣṭavya: gerundive, 'is to be offered'; yaṣṭavyam: nom. sg. neut.; simply joined with eva, final -m unaffected before the vowel)
indeed, only (eva+iti→eveti, a+i→e, guṇa sandhi)
thus [thinking] (closing the quoted thought)
mind (acc. sg. neut., object of samādhāya)
to compose, fix, settle (samādhāya: gerund, 'having fixed')
he, that (sa: nom. sg. masc.; the pronoun sa always drops its visarga before a following consonant)
sattva-natured, belonging to sattva (nom. sg. masc., predicate)

sentences.l: The-sacrifice by-those-not-desiring-the-fruit, prescribed-by-rule, which is offered, — '[it]-is-indeed-to-be-offered' — thus the-mind having-fixed — that [is] sattva-natured.
sentences.i: A sacrifice offered by those without desire for its fruit, performed as the rule prescribes, with the mind fixed only on 'this must be offered' — that is sattva-natured.
sentences.n: Opens the sacrifice-triad (vv. 11-13). Aphala-ākāṅkṣibhiḥ, 'by those not desiring the fruit' (a+ā→ā within the compound), echoes the poem's standing teaching on action without regard for its results (cf. 2.47); vidhi-dṛṣṭaḥ, 'as prescribed by rule', ties proper performance to scripture, as verse 1 raised and 16.24 already taught. Yaṣṭavyam eva iti manaḥ samādhāya, 'having fixed the mind on "it is simply to be offered"', names duty performed for its own sake as the mark of sattva. Note the visarga elided (with hiatus retained) before a following vowel in य/इज्यते — an epic-verse option already flagged at 16.1.

sentences.t:
अभिसंधाय तु फलं दम्भार्थमपि चैव यत् ।
इज्यते भरतश्रेष्ठ तं यज्ञं विद्धि राजसम् ॥
sentences.tr:
abhisaṃdhāya tu phalam dambha-artham api ca eva yat |
ijyate bharata-śreṣṭha tam yajñam viddhi rājasam ||

morph.gloss: to aim at, have in view, intend (abhisaṃdhāya: gerund, 'having aimed at')
but
fruit, result (acc. sg. neut., object of abhisaṃdhāya)
hypocrisy, ostentation (first member; dambha+artham→dambhārtham, a+a→ā)
purpose, sake (dambha-artham: 'for the sake of ostentation', adverbial acc.; simply joined with api, final -m unaffected before the vowel)
also, even
and
indeed (ca+eva→caiva, a+e→ai)
which (nom. sg. neut. relative)
to sacrifice (ijyate: present passive 3rd sg., 'is offered')
descendant of Bharata (first member)
best (bharata-śreṣṭha: 'best of the Bharatas', vocative, addressed to Arjuna)
that (acc. sg. masc.)
sacrifice (acc. sg. masc., object of viddhi)
to know (viddhi: imperative 2nd sg., 'know!')
rajas-natured, belonging to rajas (acc. sg. masc., predicate)

sentences.l: But, aiming-at the fruit, and-indeed also for-the-sake-of-ostentation, which is offered, best-of-the-Bharatas — that sacrifice know [to be] rajas-natured.
sentences.i: But the sacrifice offered with an eye on its reward, and also for the sake of show, best of the Bharatas — know that sacrifice to be rajas-natured.
sentences.n: Abhisaṃdhāya phalam, 'having aimed at the fruit', directly opposes verse 11's aphala-ākāṅkṣibhiḥ; dambha-artham, 'for the sake of ostentation', names the vice condemned repeatedly in chapter 16 (16.4, 17-18) now shown at work in ritual itself.

sentences.t:
विधिहीनमसृष्टान्नं मन्त्रहीनमदक्षिणम् ।
श्रद्धाविरहितं यज्ञं तामसं परिचक्षते ॥
sentences.tr:
vidhi-hīnam a-sṛṣṭa-annam mantra-hīnam a-dakṣiṇam |
śraddhā-virahitam yajñam tāmasam paricakṣate ||

morph.gloss: injunction, [proper] rule (first member)
lacking, devoid of (vidhi-hīnam: 'lacking [proper] rule', acc. sg. masc., predicate; simply joined with the following word, final -m unaffected before the vowel)
not given, not distributed (from sṛj; first member; a-sṛṣṭa+annam→asṛṣṭānnam, a+a→ā)
food (a-sṛṣṭa-annam: 'without the giving-out of food', acc. sg. masc., predicate)
a Vedic mantra, sacred formula (first member)
lacking, devoid of (mantra-hīnam: 'lacking [the proper] mantras', acc. sg. masc., predicate; simply joined with the following word, final -m unaffected before the vowel)
without [the priestly] fee (from dakṣiṇā, 'a fee to a priest') (a-dakṣiṇam: acc. sg. masc., predicate)
faith (first member)
devoid of, lacking (past participle of vi-rah; śraddhā-virahitam: 'devoid of faith', acc. sg. masc., predicate)
sacrifice (acc. sg. masc., object of paricakṣate)
tamas-natured, belonging to tamas (acc. sg. masc., predicate)
to call, declare, describe (paricakṣate: present middle 3rd pl., 'they call')

sentences.l: Lacking-rule, without-the-giving-of-food, lacking-mantras, without-the-priestly-fee, devoid-of-faith — that sacrifice they call tamas-natured.
sentences.i: A sacrifice that ignores the proper procedure, gives out no food, lacks the mantras, offers no fee to the priests, and is without faith — that they call tamas-natured.
sentences.n: Closes the sacrifice-triad. A-sṛṣṭa-annam, 'without the giving-out of food' (the customary distribution of food or alms at a sacrifice, here omitted), and a-dakṣiṇam, 'without the priestly fee' (dakṣiṇā, the payment due the officiating priests), name specific lapses in proper form; śraddhā-virahitam, 'devoid of faith', closes the list by naming the very quality the chapter opened by asking about (verse 1) — a sacrifice performed with fervor but without proper form and without faith is, in the end, tamas-natured.

sentences.t:
देवद्विजगुरुप्राज्ञपूजनं शौचमार्जवम् ।
ब्रह्मचर्यमहिंसा च शारीरं तप उच्यते ॥
sentences.tr:
deva-dvija-guru-prājña-pūjanam śaucam ārjavam |
brahmacaryam ahiṃsā ca śārīram tapaḥ ucyate ||

morph.gloss: a god (first member)
twice-born, a brahmin (second member)
a teacher, an elder (third member)
the wise, a sage (fourth member)
worship, reverence, honoring (deva-dvija-guru-prājña-pūjanam: 'reverence for gods, brahmins, teachers, and the wise', nom. sg. neut., list item)
purity, cleanliness (nom. sg. neut., list item; simply joined with ārjavam, final -m unaffected before the vowel)
uprightness, straightforwardness (nom. sg. neut., list item)
celibacy, sexual restraint (lit. 'conduct proper to Vedic study'; nom. sg. neut., list item; simply joined with ahiṃsā, final -m unaffected before the vowel)
non-violence, non-injury (nom. sg. fem., list item)
and
bodily, of the body (adj. from śarīra; nom. sg. neut., predicate agreeing with tapas)

austerity (nom. sg. neut., subject; its own visarga simply drops before the following vowel u- of ucyate, hiatus retained — an accepted epic-verse option, already noted at 16.1's svādhyāyas tapa ārjavam)
to speak, say (ucyate: present passive 3rd sg., 'is called')

sentences.l: Reverence-for-gods-brahmins-teachers-and-the-wise, purity, [and] uprightness; celibacy and non-violence — [this] austerity [is] called bodily.
sentences.i: Reverence for gods, brahmins, teachers, and the wise; purity, uprightness, celibacy, and non-violence — this is called austerity of the body.
sentences.n: Opens the austerity-section (vv. 14-19), first classified by where the effort is made — bodily (śārīra, this verse), verbal (vāṅmaya, v. 15), mental (mānasa, v. 16) — before being classified again by guṇa at verses 17-19. Dvija, 'twice-born', means a brahmin (as at 1.7's dvijottama); brahmacarya, literally 'conduct proper to Vedic study', is translated here as 'celibacy', the ascetic practice of sexual restraint it denotes, distinct from brahman itself, which stays untranslated. Tapa ucyate shows a visarga fully elided before the following vowel, with the hiatus kept rather than the vowels fusing — an accepted option in epic verse, already flagged at 16.1's svādhyāyas tapa ārjavam.

sentences.t:
अनुद्वेगकरं वाक्यं सत्यं प्रियहितं च यत् ।
स्वाध्यायाभ्यसनं चैव वाङ्मयं तप उच्यते ॥
sentences.tr:
an-udvega-karam vākyam satyam priya-hitam ca yat |
svādhyāya-abhyasanam ca eva vāṅ-mayam tapaḥ ucyate ||

morph.gloss: not distressing, causing no agitation (first member; a+u→an- before the vowel)
making, causing (an-udvega-karam: 'not causing distress', nom. sg. neut., adj. agreeing with vākyam)
speech, an utterance (nom. sg. neut., list item)
true, truthful (nom. sg. neut., adj. agreeing with vākyam)
pleasant, agreeable (first member)
beneficial, wholesome (priya-hitam: 'pleasant and beneficial', nom. sg. neut., adj. agreeing with vākyam)
and
that which (yat: nom. sg. neut. relative, closing the description of vākyam)
study, recitation of one's own [portion of the] Veda (first member; svādhyāya+abhyasanam→svādhyāyābhyasanam, a+a→ā)
repeated practice, exercise, habituation (svādhyāya-abhyasanam: 'the regular practice of [Vedic] recitation', nom. sg. neut., list item)
and
indeed (ca+eva→caiva, a+e→ai)
speech (first member; c+m-→ṅ+m-)
made of, consisting of (vāṅ-mayam: 'made of speech, verbal', nom. sg. neut., predicate agreeing with tapaḥ)
austerity (nom. sg. neut., subject; visarga elided before the vowel u- of ucyate, hiatus retained, as at verse 14)
to say (ucyate: present passive 3rd sg., 'is called')

sentences.l: Speech not-causing-distress, truthful, and pleasant-and-beneficial, and-indeed the-regular-practice-of-[Vedic]-recitation — [this] austerity [is] called verbal.
sentences.i: Speech that causes no distress, that is truthful, pleasant, and beneficial, together with the regular recitation of one's own scriptures — this is called austerity of speech.
sentences.n: The second of the three bodily/verbal/mental divisions. Svādhyāya, 'the recitation of one's own [portion of the] Veda', is the daily discipline already named at 16.1; vāṅ-mayam, 'made of speech' (vāc+maya, with c assimilating to ṅ before m), names the whole category. As at verse 14, tapa ucyate again shows the visarga-elision-with-hiatus pattern.

sentences.t:
मनः प्रसादः सौम्यत्वं मौनमात्मविनिग्रहः ।
भावसंशुद्धिरित्येतत्तपो मानसमुच्यते ॥
sentences.tr:
manaḥ prasādaḥ saumyatvam maunam ātma-vinigrahaḥ |
bhāva-saṃśuddhiḥ iti etat tapaḥ mānasam ucyate ||

morph.gloss: mind (manaḥ: nom. sg. neut., functioning attributively with prasādaḥ, 'serenity of mind')
serenity, clarity, tranquility (nom. sg. masc., list item, 'serenity of mind')
gentleness, mildness (abstract noun from saumya + -tva; nom. sg. neut., list item)
silence (nom. sg. neut., list item; simply joined with the following word, final -m unaffected before the vowel)
self (first member)
restraint, mastery (ātma-vinigrahaḥ: 'self-restraint', nom. sg. masc., list item)
state, nature, inner disposition (first member)
purity, purification (bhāva-saṃśuddhiḥ: 'purity of one's inner nature', nom. sg. fem., list item; -iḥ+i-→-ir i-)
thus (marking the close of the list; iti+etat→ityetat, -i+e-→-y e-)
this (nom. sg. neut., resuming the list as a whole)
austerity (tapaḥ: nom. sg. neut., subject; its own visarga becomes -o before the voiced m- of the following word)
mental, of the mind (nom. sg. neut., predicate; simply joined with ucyate, final -m unaffected before the vowel)
to say (ucyate: present passive 3rd sg., 'is called')

sentences.l: Serenity of-mind, gentleness, silence, self-restraint, and purity-of-[one's-own]-nature — this austerity [is] called mental.
sentences.i: Serenity of mind, gentleness, silence, self-mastery, and purity of one's inner disposition — this is called austerity of the mind.
sentences.n: Closes the threefold division of austerity by location. Manaḥ prasādaḥ, 'serenity of mind', is written as two separate words rather than a compound but functions as a single idea; bhāva-saṃśuddhiḥ, 'purity of one's inner nature/disposition', closes the list — note bhāva here, like sattva at verse 3, names a person's general inner state rather than any single guṇa. With the threefold classification by location now complete, verses 17-19 classify this same threefold austerity again, this time by guṇa.

sentences.t:
श्रद्धया परया तप्तं तपस्तत्त्रिविधं नरैः ।
अफलाकाङ्क्षिभिर्युक्तैः सात्त्विकं परिचक्षते ॥
sentences.tr:
śraddhayā parayā taptam tapaḥ tat tri-vidham naraiḥ |
a-phala-ākāṅkṣibhiḥ yuktaiḥ sāttvikam paricakṣate ||

morph.gloss: faith (instr. sg. 'with faith')
supreme, highest (parayā: instr. sg. fem., agreeing with śraddhayā)
to practice, perform [with effort] (tapta: past participle; nom. sg. neut., predicate, 'practiced')
austerity (tapaḥ: nom. sg. neut., subject; -aḥ+t-→-as t-)
that (tat: nom. sg. neut., referring back to the threefold austerity of verses 14-16; dental+dental, written joined)
threefold (trividham: nom. sg. neut., agreeing with tapaḥ)
a man (instr. pl., 'by men')
fruitless, without [regard for] the fruit (first member; a-phala+ākāṅkṣibhiḥ→aphalākāṅkṣibhiḥ, a+ā→ā)
desiring (a-phala-ākāṅkṣibhiḥ: 'by those not desiring the fruit', instr. pl. masc., agreeing with naraiḥ; ākāṅkṣibhiḥ+yuktaiḥ→ākāṅkṣibhiryuktaiḥ, -iḥ+y-→-ir y-)
joined, disciplined, engaged (yuktaiḥ: instr. pl., agreeing with naraiḥ)
sattva-natured, belonging to sattva (nom. sg. neut., predicate agreeing with tapaḥ)
to call, declare (paricakṣate: present middle 3rd pl.)

sentences.l: With-supreme-faith practiced, that threefold austerity, by-men without-desire-for-the-fruit, disciplined — [this] they call sattva-natured.
sentences.i: That threefold austerity, practiced with the highest faith by men who are free from desire for its fruit and disciplined in themselves — this they call sattva-natured.
sentences.n: Tat trividham, 'that threefold [austerity]', reaches back to the śārīra/vāṅmaya/mānasa triad of verses 14-16, now reclassified — like sacrifice before it (vv. 11-13) — into its sattva-, rajas- and tamas-natured forms. Aphala-ākāṅkṣibhiḥ yuktaiḥ, 'by men without desire for the fruit, disciplined', echoes verse 11's identical phrase for sacrifice; śraddhayā parayā, 'with supreme faith', returns the chapter explicitly to its opening theme.

sentences.t:
सत्कारमानपूजार्थं तपो दम्भेन चैव यत् ।
क्रियते तदिह प्रोक्तं राजसं चलमध्रुवम् ॥
sentences.tr:
satkāra-māna-pūjā-artham tapaḥ dambhena ca eva yat |
kriyate tat iha proktam rājasam calam a-dhruvam ||

morph.gloss: honor, esteem, hospitable reception (first member)
respect, regard (second member)
reverence, worship (third member; pūjā+artham→pūjārtham, ā+a→ā)
purpose, sake (satkāra-māna-pūjā-artham: 'for the sake of honor, respect and reverence [from others]', adverbial acc.)
austerity (nom. sg. neut., subject; -aḥ before d-→-o)
hypocrisy, ostentation (instr. sg. 'with hypocrisy')
and
indeed (ca+eva→caiva, a+e→ai)
which (nom. sg. neut. relative)
to do, perform (kriyate: present passive 3rd sg.)
that (tat: nom. sg. neut.; -t+i-→-d i-)
here, in this world
declared, called (prokta: past participle; nom. sg. neut., predicate)
rajas-natured, belonging to rajas (nom. sg. neut., predicate)
unsteady, fickle (calam: nom. sg. neut., predicate; simply joined with the following word, final -m unaffected before the vowel)
unstable, not lasting (nom. sg. neut., predicate)

sentences.l: For-the-sake-of-honor-respect-and-reverence, and-indeed also with-hypocrisy, austerity which is performed — that here [is] declared rajas-natured, unsteady, unstable.
sentences.i: Austerity performed for the sake of honor, respect, and reverence, and out of hypocrisy — that is declared here to be rajas-natured, unsteady and impermanent.
sentences.n: Satkāra-māna-pūjā-artham, 'for the sake of honor, respect and reverence [from others]', names the desire for outward recognition, paired with dambhena, 'with hypocrisy' — the same vice named at verse 12 for sacrifice. Calam a-dhruvam, 'unsteady, unstable', judges the fruit of such austerity as fleeting, unlike sattva's lasting result.

sentences.t:
मूढग्राहेणात्मनो यत्पीडया क्रियते तपः ।
परस्योत्सादनार्थं वा तत्तामसमुदाहृतम् ॥
sentences.tr:
mūḍha-grāheṇa ātmanaḥ yat pīḍayā kriyate tapaḥ |
parasya utsādana-artham vā tat tāmasam udāhṛtam ||

morph.gloss: deluded, foolish (from muh; first member)
a grasp, a conviction, an obstinate notion (mūḍha-grāheṇa: 'out of deluded obstinacy', instr. sg.; mūḍhagrāheṇa+ātmanaḥ→mūḍhagrāheṇātmanaḥ, a+ā→ā)
oneself (ātmanaḥ: gen. sg., governed by pīḍayā, 'the affliction of oneself'; -aḥ before y-→-o)
which (yat: nom. sg. neut. relative)
affliction, torment (pīḍayā: instr. sg., 'with the affliction [of oneself]')
to do, perform (kriyate: present passive 3rd sg.)
austerity (nom. sg. neut., subject)
another [person] (parasya: gen. sg. 'of another'; parasya+utsādana→parasyotsādana, a+u→o)
destruction, injury, ruin (second member)
purpose, sake (parasya utsādana-artham: 'for the sake of the destruction of another', adverbial acc.)
or
that (tat: nom. sg. neut., subject; dental+dental, written joined)
tamas-natured, belonging to tamas (tāmasam: nom. sg. neut., predicate; simply joined with the following word, final -m unaffected before the vowel)
declared, stated (past participle of ud-āhṛ; nom. sg. neut., predicate)

sentences.l: Which austerity, out-of-deluded-obstinacy, with-the-affliction-of-oneself, is performed, or for-the-sake-of-the-destruction-of-another — that [is] declared tamas-natured.
sentences.i: Austerity performed out of deluded stubbornness, through self-torment, or in order to destroy another — that is declared to be tamas-natured.
sentences.n: Closes the austerity-triad. Mūḍha-grāheṇa, 'out of deluded obstinacy' (grāha, 'a grasp, a fixed and mistaken conviction'), recalls the self-torturing ascetics condemned already at verses 5-6; parasya utsādana-artham, 'for the sake of destroying another', names austerity turned to malice or black magic — the darkest of the three.

sentences.t:
दातव्यमिति यद्दानं दीयतेऽनुपकारिणे ।
देशे काले च पात्रे च तद्दानं सात्त्विकं स्मृतम् ॥
sentences.tr:
dātavyam iti yat dānam dīyate anupakāriṇe |
deśe kāle ca pātre ca tat dānam sāttvikam smṛtam ||

sentences.l: '[It]-is-to-be-given' — thus, which gift is given to-one-who-cannot-repay, in-the-[right]-place and-[right]-time and to-a-worthy-recipient — that gift [is] held sattva-natured.
sentences.i: A gift given because 'it is simply right to give', to someone who can make no return, at the proper place and time and to a worthy recipient — that gift is held to be sattva-natured.
sentences.n: Opens the giving-triad (vv. 20-22), the last of the four topics named in verse 7. An-upakāriṇe, 'to one who cannot repay', rules out gift-giving as disguised exchange; deśe kāle ca pātre ca, 'in the [right] place and time and to a worthy recipient', names the three traditional conditions of a proper gift. Dātavyam iti, 'because it is simply to be given', echoes verse 11's yaṣṭavyam eva iti — duty performed because it is right, the recurring mark of sattva throughout this chapter.

sentences.t:
यत्तु प्रत्युपकारार्थं फलमुद्दिश्य वा पुनः ।
दीयते च परिक्लिष्टं तद्दानं राजसं स्मृतम् ॥

sentences.l: But which, for-the-sake-of-a-return-favor, or again aiming-at [future] reward, is given, and given-reluctantly — that gift [is] held rajas-natured.
sentences.i: But a gift given in hope of some favor in return, or again with an eye on the reward to come, and given grudgingly — that gift is held to be rajas-natured.
sentences.n: Prati-upakāra-artham, 'for the sake of a return favor', directly negates verse 20's an-upakāriṇe; pari-kliṣṭam, 'given with reluctance, grudgingly', marks the giver's inner state as much as the outer act.

sentences.t:
अदेशकाले यद्दानमपात्रेभ्यश्च दीयते ।
असत्कृतमवज्ञातं तत्तामसमुदाहृतम् ॥

a-sat-kṛtam avajñātam tat tāmasam udāhṛtam ||

sentences.l: At-a-wrong-place-and-time which gift, to-unworthy-recipients, is given, without-proper-respect and with-contempt — that [is] declared tamas-natured.
sentences.i: A gift given at the wrong place and time, to unworthy recipients, without respect and with contempt — that is declared to be tamas-natured.
sentences.n: Closes the giving-triad, and with it the whole enumerative half of the chapter (faith, worship, food, sacrifice, austerity, giving), by negating each term of verse 20 in turn: a-deśa-kāle against deśe kāle (the single privative a- here negating the whole pair, not deśa alone), a-pātrebhyaḥ against pātre, a-sat-kṛtam avajñātam, 'given without respect and with contempt', against the implicit honor of a proper gift. Verse 23 turns to the chapter's final and most demanding topic: the threefold name of brahman.

sentences.t:
ॐतत्सदिति निर्देशो ब्रह्मणस्त्रिविधः स्मृतः ।
ब्राह्मणास्तेन वेदाश्च यज्ञाश्च विहिताः पुरा ॥
sentences.tr:
oṃ tat sat iti nirdeśaḥ brahmaṇaḥ tri-vidhaḥ smṛtaḥ |
brāhmaṇāḥ tena vedāḥ ca yajñāḥ ca vihitāḥ purā ||

Tat, 'That', the second name (tat: nom. sg. neut.; dental+dental, written joined)
Sat, 'Being, the Real', the third name (sat: nom. sg. neut.; -t+i-→-d i-)
thus, [these three] (closing the enumeration)
designation, indication, pointing-out (nirdeśaḥ: nom. sg. masc., subject; -aḥ before b-→-o)
brahman, kept untranslated per convention (brahmaṇaḥ: gen. sg., 'of brahman'; -aḥ+t-→-as t-)
threefold (trividhaḥ: nom. sg. masc., predicate)
to hold in mind, remember (smṛta: past participle, 'is held [to be], is recorded'; nom. sg. masc., predicate)
a brahmin (brāhmaṇāḥ: nom. pl. masc., subject; -āḥ+t-→-ās t-)
by that, by it (tena: instr. sg. neut., referring to the threefold designation just named)
the Veda (vedāḥ: nom. pl. masc., subject; -āḥ+c-→-āś c-)
and
sacrifice (yajñāḥ: nom. pl. masc., subject; -āḥ+c-→-āś c-)
and
ordained, established (vihita: past participle; nom. pl. masc., predicate)
formerly, of old (adverb)

sentences.l: 'Oṃ', 'Tat', 'Sat' — thus, the-designation of-brahman threefold [is] held; by-that were-brahmins, and-the-Vedas, and-sacrifices ordained, of-old.
sentences.i: 'Oṃ', 'Tat', 'Sat' — this is remembered as the threefold designation of brahman. By it, in ancient times, brahmins, the Vedas, and sacrifices were established.
sentences.n: This opens the chapter's closing section (vv. 23-28) and names its whole subject in one breath: all four words of the verse's first line are written as a single fused token (oṃ+tat+sat+iti, the last junction -t+i-→-d i-). Brahman, which cannot itself be spoken, is traditionally held to have this threefold name (nirdeśa, 'designation, pointing-out'): oṃ, the sacred syllable uttered at the start of Vedic recitation and rites; tat, 'That', the pronoun by which the Upaniṣads point to brahman beyond all qualities (as in tat tvam asi); and sat, 'Being, the Real', brahman under the aspect of pure existence. Each of the three is then treated in turn — oṃ in verse 24, tat in verse 25, sat in verses 26-27. Brāhmaṇāḥ ... vihitāḥ purā, '[brahmins, Vedas and sacrifices] were established of old', states that the whole Vedic order draws its authority from this threefold name of brahman. Brahman stays untranslated per convention; oṃ, tat and sat, being the very subject of this passage, are likewise left untranslated here as its three names — unlike sat/asat from verse 26 on, where the same word is used in its ordinary sense and is translated (see the note to verse 26).

sentences.t:
तस्मादोमित्युदाहृत्य यज्ञदानतपःक्रियाः ।
प्रवर्तन्ते विधानोक्ताः सततं ब्रह्मवादिनाम् ॥
sentences.tr:
tasmāt oṃ iti udāhṛtya yajña-dāna-tapaḥ-kriyāḥ |
pravartante vidhāna-uktāḥ satatam brahma-vādinām ||

sacrifice (first member)
giving (second member)
austerity (third member)
a rite, an act (yajña-dāna-tapaḥ-kriyāḥ: 'the rites of sacrifice, giving and austerity', nom. pl. fem., subject)
to proceed, go forward, be carried out (pravartante: present middle 3rd pl.)
ordinance, injunction, rule (first member; vidhāna+uktāḥ→vidhānoktāḥ, a+u→o)
declared, prescribed (past participle of vac; vidhāna-uktāḥ: 'prescribed by rule', nom. pl. fem., predicate agreeing with kriyāḥ)

sentences.l: Therefore, 'Oṃ' having-uttered, the-rites-of-sacrifice-giving-and-austerity, prescribed-by-rule, proceed constantly, of-those-who-expound-brahman.
sentences.i: So, with 'Oṃ' uttered first, the rites of sacrifice, giving, and austerity, as scripture prescribes, are constantly carried out among those who expound brahman.
sentences.n: Treats oṃ, the first of the three names just given. Brahma-vādinām, 'of those who expound/uphold brahman', names followers of Vedic tradition, whose rites are still customarily prefaced with the utterance of oṃ; tasmāt, 'therefore', ties this directly back to verse 23's naming of oṃ as brahman's first designation. Brahman again kept untranslated; oṃ likewise, as the subject just named.

sentences.t:
तदित्यनभिसन्धाय फलं यज्ञतपःक्रियाः ।
दानक्रियाश्च विविधाः क्रियन्ते मोक्षकाङ्क्षिभिः ॥
sentences.tr:

dāna-kriyāḥ ca vividhāḥ kriyante mokṣa-kāṅkṣibhiḥ ||

thus [uttering] (closing the quoted word; iti+an-→ityan-, -i+a-→-y a-)
without aiming at, without regard for (an-abhisaṃdhāya: gerund of abhi-sam-dhā with the negative prefix an-, 'without aiming at')
fruit, reward (acc. sg. neut., object of anabhisaṃdhāya)
sacrifice (first member)
austerity (second member)
a rite (yajña-tapaḥ-kriyāḥ: 'the rites of sacrifice and austerity', nom. pl. fem., subject)
giving (first member)
a rite, an act (dāna-kriyāḥ: 'the rites of giving', nom. pl. fem., subject; -āḥ+c-→-āś c-)
and
various, of various kinds (nom. pl. fem., adj.)
to do, perform (kriyante: present passive 3rd pl.)
liberation (first member)
desiring, wishing for (mokṣa-kāṅkṣibhiḥ: 'by those desiring liberation', instr. pl. masc., agent)

sentences.l: 'Tat' — thus, not-aiming-at the fruit, the-rites-of-sacrifice-and-austerity, and-the-rites-of-giving, various, are-performed by-those-desiring-liberation.
sentences.i: Uttering 'Tat', and without an eye on the fruit, those who desire liberation perform the various rites of sacrifice, austerity, and giving.
sentences.n: Treats tat, the second name. Tat iti anabhisaṃdhāya phalam, 'thinking "Tat", without aiming at the fruit', means performing the rite while inwardly identifying the act with brahman itself, so that its fruit is renounced — the same teaching on desireless action given throughout chapters 2-3 and again at 4.24's brahma-arpaṇaṃ brahma haviḥ. Mokṣa-kāṅkṣibhiḥ, 'by those desiring liberation', names the aim of such renunciation directly.

sentences.t:
सद्भावे साधुभावे च सदित्येतत्प्रयुज्यते ।
प्रशस्ते कर्मणि तथा सच्छब्दः पार्थ युज्यते ॥
sentences.tr:
sat-bhāve sādhu-bhāve ca sat iti etat prayujyate |
praśaste karmaṇi tathā sat-śabdaḥ pārtha yujyate ||

a sense, a meaning, a condition (sat-bhāve: 'in the sense of being, of existing', loc. sg.)
good, excellent, virtuous (first member)
a sense, a meaning (sādhu-bhāve: 'in the sense of goodness, of excellence', loc. sg.)
and

thus, [as the word] (iti+etat→ityetat, -i+e-→-y e-)
this (nom. sg. neut., 'this [word "sat"]')
to use, employ (prayujyate: present passive 3rd sg., 'is used')
praiseworthy, commendable (past participle of pra-śaṃs) (praśaste: loc. sg., 'in a praiseworthy [action]')
action, a deed (loc. sg.)
likewise, also
'sat' (first member; sat+śabdaḥ→sacchabdaḥ, -t+ś-→-c ch-)
a word (sat-śabdaḥ: 'the word "sat"', nom. sg. masc., subject)
son of Pṛthā, Arjuna (vocative)
to apply, employ, join (yujyate: present passive 3rd sg., 'is applied')

sentences.l: In-the-sense-of-being and in-the-sense-of-goodness — thus this [word] 'sat' is-used; and, likewise, in-a-praiseworthy action, the-word-'sat' is-applied, son-of-Pṛthā.
sentences.i: In the sense of reality and in the sense of excellence — that is how the word 'sat' is used; and it is applied, Pārtha, to a praiseworthy action as well.
sentences.n: Opens the closing treatment of sat, the third name (vv. 26-27), by distinguishing its two basic senses: sad-bhāve, 'in the sense of being, of existing' (its plain ontological use), and sādhu-bhāve, 'in the sense of goodness, of excellence' (its evaluative use) — and further, of a praśaste karmaṇi, 'a praiseworthy action'. From this point on, unlike the formula oṃ tat sat of verses 23-24 (kept untranslated there as brahman's own name), sat names an ordinary word under analysis and is accordingly translated, here and in verses 27-28, as 'being/reality' or 'good' according to context, per the pipeline's settled practice for this chapter. Sandhi: sad-bhāve is sat+bhāve (-t+bh-→-d bh-); sac-chabdaḥ is sat+śabdaḥ (-t+ś-→-c ch-), the same assimilation already seen at 16.24's tasmāc-chāstram.

sentences.t:
यज्ञे तपसि दाने च स्थितिः सदिति चोच्यते ।
कर्म चैव तदर्थीयं सदित्येवाभिधीयते ॥

karma ca eva tad-arthīyam sat iti eva abhidhīyate ||

and

'sat' (quoted; sat+iti→sad iti, -t+i-→-d i-)

sentences.i: Steadfastness in sacrifice, austerity, and giving is also called 'sat'; and any action directed to that end is likewise termed 'sat'.
sentences.n: Closes the sat-section. Sthitiḥ, 'steadfastness, constancy' — perseverance in the very practices classified by guṇa in verses 11-22 — is itself called sat; and tad-arthīyam karma, 'action directed to that [same] end' (i.e. done for the sake of, or in connection with, the sacrifice, austerity and giving just named in this same verse's first line — not a fresh reference to verse 25's mokṣa), is likewise so termed. The section ties the abstract oṃ-tat-sat formula of verses 23-24 back to the concrete triads of sacrifice, austerity and giving that filled most of the chapter.

sentences.t:
अश्रद्धया हुतं दत्तं तपस्तप्तं कृतं च यत् ।
असदित्युच्यते पार्थ न च तत्प्रेत्य नो इह ॥

sentences.l: Without-faith [what is] offered, given, austerity practiced, and done — that is-called 'asat', son-of-Pṛthā; and that [is] not, hereafter, nor indeed here.
sentences.i: Whatever is offered, given, or done, or whatever austerity is practiced without faith — that is called 'asat', Pārtha; it is nothing, neither in the world to come nor in this one.
sentences.n: The chapter's close, naming asat, the negative counterpart of sat: whatever act — hutam, dattam, tapaḥ taptam, kṛtam, 'offered, given, austerity practiced, done' — is performed a-śraddhayā, 'without faith', is asat, worthless; and tat na ... pretya no iha, 'that is nothing, neither hereafter nor here' (no read as na+u, an emphatic 'nor indeed', a+u→o, guṇa sandhi). The verse closes the ring begun at the chapter's very first line (verse 1's yajante śraddhayā anvitāḥ), confirming that śraddhā, faith, is the one condition running beneath every triad the chapter has drawn — food, sacrifice, austerity, giving, and now even the very name of brahman.

glossary.तामसी: tāmasī — tāmasa — tamas-natured, belonging to tamas (nom. sg. fem.; tamas kept untranslated)

glossary.शृणु: śṛṇu — śru — to hear (śṛṇu: imperative 2nd sg., 'hear!')
glossary.सत्त्वानुरूपा: sattva-anurūpā — sattva — one's own being, disposition (here the individual's inner nature or constitution, not the guṇa named in its narrower sense — see note; first member); anurūpa — conforming to, corresponding to (sattva-anurūpā: 'conformed to one's own nature', nom. sg. fem., predicate; a+a→ā)
glossary.सर्वस्य: sarvasya — sarva — every, all (sarvasya: gen. sg. 'of everyone, of each')
glossary.भारत: bhārata — Bhārata — descendant of Bharata, Arjuna (vocative)
glossary.श्रद्धामयोऽयं: śraddhā-mayaḥ ayam — śraddhā — faith (first member); maya — made of, consisting of (śraddhā-mayaḥ: 'made of faith', nom. sg. masc., predicate; -aḥ+a-→-o' with avagraha); idam — this (ayam: nom. sg. masc., subject)
glossary.पुरुषो: puruṣaḥ — puruṣa — a person, a man (nom. sg. masc., subject; -aḥ before y-→-o)
glossary.यो: yaḥ — yad — who (yaḥ: nom. sg. masc. relative; -aḥ before y-→-o)
glossary.यच्छ्रद्धः: yat-śraddhaḥ — yad — what, whatever (first member; -t+ś-→-c ch-); śraddha — having ... faith (bahuvrīhi compound member; yat-śraddhaḥ: 'he whose faith is what [it is]', nom. sg. masc.)

glossary.सात्त्विका: sāttvikāḥ — sāttvika — sattva-natured, belonging to sattva (nom. pl. masc.; -āḥ before d-→-ā)
glossary.देवान्यक्षरक्षांसि: devān yakṣa-rakṣāṃsi — deva — god (devān: acc. pl., object of yajante in the first clause); yakṣa — a yakṣa, a class of demigod, a nature-spirit (first member); rakṣas — a rākṣasa, a class of demon (yakṣa-rakṣāṃsi: 'yakṣas and rākṣasas', acc. pl. neut. dvandva, object of yajante understood in the second clause)
glossary.राजसाः: rājasāḥ — rājasa — rajas-natured, belonging to rajas (nom. pl. masc., subject)
glossary.प्रेतान्भूतगणांश्चान्ये: pretān bhūta-gaṇān ca anye — preta — a departed spirit, a ghost (pretān: acc. pl., object of yajante); bhūta-gaṇa — a host of bhūtas, spirits, elemental beings (bhūtagaṇān: acc. pl.; -n+c-→-ṃś c-); ca — and; anya — other (anye: nom. pl. masc., agreeing with janāḥ; ca+anye→cānye, a+a→ā)
glossary.तामसा: tāmasāḥ — tāmasa — tamas-natured, belonging to tamas (nom. pl. masc.; -āḥ before j-→-ā)
glossary.जनाः: janāḥ — jana — a person, people (nom. pl. masc., subject)
glossary.अशास्त्रविहितं: a-śāstra-vihitam — a-śāstra — not [enjoined by] scripture (first member); vihita — enjoined, ordained (past participle of vi-dhā; a-śāstra-vihitam: 'not enjoined by scripture', acc. sg. neut., agreeing with tapaḥ)
glossary.घोरं: ghoram — ghora — terrible, dreadful (acc. sg. neut.)
glossary.तप्यन्ते: tapyante — tap — to practice austerity, to torment oneself (tapyante: present middle 3rd pl.)
glossary.तपो: tapaḥ — tapas — austerity (acc. sg. neut., object of tapyante, 'practice austerity'; -aḥ before j-→-o)
glossary.दम्भाहंकारसंयुक्ताः: dambha-ahaṃkāra-saṃyuktāḥ — dambha — hypocrisy, ostentation (first member); ahaṃkāra — egotism, the sense of 'I' (second member); saṃyukta — joined with, endowed with (past participle of sam-yuj; dambha-ahaṃkāra-saṃyuktāḥ: 'joined with hypocrisy and egotism', nom. pl. masc., predicate)
glossary.कामरागबलान्विताः: kāma-rāga-bala-anvitāḥ — kāma — desire (first member); rāga — passion, attachment (second member); bala — force, power (third member; bala+anvitāḥ→balānvitāḥ, a+a→ā); anvita — possessed by, filled with (kāma-rāga-bala-anvitāḥ: 'possessed by the force of desire and passion', nom. pl. masc., predicate)

glossary.शरीरस्थं: śarīra-stham — śarīra — body (first member); stha — situated in, abiding in (śarīra-stham: 'situated in the body', acc. sg. masc., agreeing with bhūta-grāmam)
glossary.भूतग्राममचेतसः: bhūta-grāmam acetasaḥ — bhūta — element, being (first member); grāma — aggregate, multitude, host (bhūta-grāmam: 'the aggregate of [bodily] elements', acc. sg. masc., object of karṣayantaḥ); a-cetas — mindless, without understanding (acetasaḥ: nom. pl. masc., agreeing with the subject 'they', carried over from verse 5's janāḥ; bhūtagrāmam+acetasaḥ simply joined, final -m unaffected before the vowel)
glossary.मां: mām — aham — I (mām: acc. sg., object of viddhi, 'me too')
glossary.चैवान्तःशरीरस्थं: ca eva antar-śarīra-stham — ca — and; eva — indeed, too (ca+eva→caiva, a+e→ai; caiva+antar-→caivāntar-, a+a→ā); antar — within, inside (surface form antaḥ- before the unvoiced ś-; first member); śarīra — body (second member); stha — situated in, dwelling in (antar-śarīra-stham: 'dwelling within the body', acc. sg. masc., agreeing with mām)
glossary.तान्विद्ध्यासुरनिश्चयान्: tān viddhi āsura-niścayān — tad — those (tān: acc. pl., referring back to verse 5's ye janāḥ, 'those people'); vid — to know (viddhi: imperative 2nd sg., 'know!'; viddhi+āsura-→viddhyāsura-, -i+ā-→-y ā-); āsura — demonic (first member); niścaya — resolve, determination, conviction (āsura-niścayān: 'of demonic resolve', acc. pl. masc., predicate complement of tān)
glossary.आहारस्त्वपि: āhāraḥ tu api — āhāra — food (āhāraḥ: nom. sg. masc., subject; -aḥ+t-→-as t-); tu — but, now (particle; tu+api→tvapi, -u+a-→-v a-, yaṇ sandhi); api — also, indeed
glossary.त्रिविधो: trividhaḥ — tri-vidha — threefold (trividhaḥ: nom. sg. masc., predicate; -aḥ before bh-→-o)
glossary.प्रियः: priyaḥ — priya — dear, pleasing (nom. sg. masc., predicate)
glossary.यज्ञस्तपस्तथा: yajñaḥ tapaḥ tathā — yajña — sacrifice (yajñaḥ: nom. sg. masc.; -aḥ+t-→-as t-); tapas — austerity (tapaḥ: nom. sg. neut.; -aḥ+t-→-as t-); tathā — likewise
glossary.भेदमिमं: bhedam imam — bheda — distinction, difference (bhedam: acc. sg. masc., object of śṛṇu; simply joined with imam, final -m unaffected before the vowel); idam — this (imam: acc. sg. masc.)
glossary.आयुःसत्त्वबलारोग्यसुखप्रीतिविवर्धनाः: āyuḥ-sattva-bala-ārogya-sukha-prīti-vivardhanāḥ — āyus — lifespan, length of life (first member); sattva — vitality, vigor, strength of mind (here a secondary sense of the word, not the guṇa named as such — see note; second member); bala — strength (third member; bala+ārogya→balārogya, a+ā→ā); ārogya — health, freedom from illness (fourth member); sukha — happiness (fifth member); prīti — satisfaction, pleasure (sixth member); vivardhana — increasing, promoting (āyuḥ-sattva-bala-ārogya-sukha-prīti-vivardhanāḥ: 'increasing lifespan, vitality, strength, health, happiness and satisfaction', nom. pl. masc., predicate agreeing with āhārāḥ)
glossary.रस्याः: rasyāḥ — rasya — savory, juicy, full of flavor (nom. pl. masc.)
glossary.स्निग्धाः: snigdhāḥ — snigdha — unctuous, smooth, rich (nom. pl. masc.)
glossary.स्थिरा: sthirāḥ — sthira — firm, substantial, lasting (nom. pl. masc.; -āḥ before h-→-ā)
glossary.हृद्या: hṛdyāḥ — hṛdya — agreeable to the heart, pleasing (nom. pl. masc.; -āḥ before ā-→-ā)
glossary.आहाराः: āhārāḥ — āhāra — food (nom. pl. masc., subject)
glossary.सात्त्विकप्रियाः: sāttvika-priyāḥ — sāttvika — sattva-natured, belonging to sattva (first member); priya — dear to (sāttvika-priyāḥ: 'dear to the sattva-natured', nom. pl. masc., predicate)
glossary.कट्वम्ललवणात्युष्णतीक्ष्णरूक्षविदाहिनः: kaṭu-amla-lavaṇa-ati-uṣṇa-tīkṣṇa-rūkṣa-vidāhinaḥ — kaṭu — pungent, bitter (first member; kaṭu+amla→kaṭvamla, -u+a-→-v a-, yaṇ sandhi); amla — sour (second member); lavaṇa — salty (third member; lavaṇa+ati→lavaṇāti, a+a→ā); ati — excessively, very (fourth member; ati+uṣṇa→atyuṣṇa, -i+u-→-y u-, yaṇ sandhi); uṣṇa — hot (fifth member); tīkṣṇa — sharp, acrid (sixth member); rūkṣa — dry, rough (seventh member); vidāhin — burning, causing a burning sensation (kaṭu-amla-lavaṇa-ati-uṣṇa-tīkṣṇa-rūkṣa-vidāhinaḥ: 'pungent, sour, salty, excessively hot, sharp, dry, burning', nom. pl. masc., predicate)
glossary.आहारा: āhārāḥ — āhāra — food (nom. pl. masc., subject; -āḥ before r-→-ā)
glossary.राजसस्येष्टा: rājasasya iṣṭāḥ — rājasa — the rajas-natured [person] (rājasasya: gen. sg. 'of the rajas-natured'; rājasasya+iṣṭāḥ→rājasasyeṣṭāḥ, a+i→e, guṇa sandhi); iṣṭa — desired, favored (past participle of iṣ; iṣṭāḥ: nom. pl. masc., predicate; -āḥ before d-→-ā)
glossary.दुःखशोकामयप्रदाः: duḥkha-śoka-āmaya-pradāḥ — duḥkha — pain, suffering (first member); śoka — grief (second member; śoka+āmaya→śokāmaya, a+ā→ā); āmaya — disease, sickness (third member); prada — causing, bestowing (duḥkha-śoka-āmaya-pradāḥ: 'causing pain, grief and disease', nom. pl. masc., predicate)
glossary.यातयामं: yāta-yāmam — yāta — gone, passed (first member); yāma — a watch, a period of time (yāta-yāmam: 'past its [proper] time, stale', nom. sg. neut., agreeing with bhojanam)
glossary.गतरसं: gata-rasam — gata — gone (first member); rasa — flavor, savour, juice (gata-rasam: 'having lost its flavor, flat', nom. sg. neut.)

glossary.यत्: yat — yad — that which (yat: nom. sg. neut. relative, resuming as bhojanam, closing the description)
glossary.उच्छिष्टमपि: ucchiṣṭam api — ucchiṣṭa — a remnant of a meal, food left over, ritually impure (ucchiṣṭam: nom. sg. neut.; simply joined with api, final -m unaffected before the vowel); api — also, even
glossary.चामेध्यं: ca amedhyam — ca — and (ca+amedhyam→cāmedhyam, a+a→ā); a-medhya — impure, unfit for sacrifice (amedhyam: nom. sg. neut.)
glossary.भोजनं: bhojanam — bhojana — food (nom. sg. neut., subject)
glossary.तामसप्रियम्: tāmasa-priyam — tāmasa — tamas-natured, belonging to tamas (first member); priya — dear to (tāmasa-priyam: 'dear to the tamas-natured', nom. sg. neut., predicate)
glossary.अफलाकाङ्क्षिभिर्यज्ञो: a-phala-ākāṅkṣibhiḥ yajñaḥ — a-phala — fruitless, without [regard for] the fruit (first member; a-phala+ākāṅkṣibhiḥ→aphalākāṅkṣibhiḥ, a+ā→ā); ākāṅkṣin — desiring, wishing for (a-phala-ākāṅkṣibhiḥ: 'by those not desiring the fruit', instr. pl. masc.; ākāṅkṣibhiḥ+yajñaḥ→ākāṅkṣibhiryajñaḥ, -iḥ+y-→-ir y-); yajña — sacrifice (yajñaḥ: nom. sg. masc., subject; -aḥ before v-→-o)
glossary.विधिदृष्टो: vidhi-dṛṣṭaḥ — vidhi — injunction, rule (first member); dṛṣṭa — seen, hence prescribed (past participle of dṛś; vidhi-dṛṣṭaḥ: 'as prescribed by rule', nom. sg. masc., predicate; -aḥ before y-→-o)
glossary.य: yaḥ — yad — which (yaḥ: nom. sg. masc. relative; visarga elided before the following vowel i-, hiatus retained — an accepted epic-verse option, already noted at 16.1's svādhyāyas tapa ārjavam)
glossary.इज्यते: ijyate — yaj — to sacrifice (ijyate: present passive 3rd sg., 'is offered')
glossary.यष्टव्यमेवेति: yaṣṭavyam eva iti — yaj — to sacrifice (yaṣṭavya: gerundive, 'is to be offered'; yaṣṭavyam: nom. sg. neut.; simply joined with eva, final -m unaffected before the vowel); eva — indeed, only (eva+iti→eveti, a+i→e, guṇa sandhi); iti — thus [thinking] (closing the quoted thought)
glossary.मनः: manaḥ — manas — mind (acc. sg. neut., object of samādhāya)
glossary.समाधाय: samādhāya — sam-ā-dhā — to compose, fix, settle (samādhāya: gerund, 'having fixed')
glossary.सात्त्विकः: sāttvikaḥ — sāttvika — sattva-natured, belonging to sattva (nom. sg. masc., predicate)
glossary.अभिसंधाय: abhisaṃdhāya — abhi-sam-dhā — to aim at, have in view, intend (abhisaṃdhāya: gerund, 'having aimed at')
glossary.फलं: phalam — phala — fruit, result (acc. sg. neut., object of abhisaṃdhāya)
glossary.दम्भार्थमपि: dambha-artham api — dambha — hypocrisy, ostentation (first member; dambha+artham→dambhārtham, a+a→ā); artha — purpose, sake (dambha-artham: 'for the sake of ostentation', adverbial acc.; simply joined with api, final -m unaffected before the vowel); api — also, even
glossary.भरतश्रेष्ठ: bharata-śreṣṭha — Bharata — descendant of Bharata (first member); śreṣṭha — best (bharata-śreṣṭha: 'best of the Bharatas', vocative, addressed to Arjuna)
glossary.यज्ञं: yajñam — yajña — sacrifice (acc. sg. masc., object of viddhi)
glossary.विद्धि: viddhi — vid — to know (viddhi: imperative 2nd sg., 'know!')
glossary.राजसम्: rājasam — rājasa — rajas-natured, belonging to rajas (acc. sg. masc., predicate)
glossary.विधिहीनमसृष्टान्नं: vidhi-hīnam a-sṛṣṭa-annam — vidhi — injunction, [proper] rule (first member); hīna — lacking, devoid of (vidhi-hīnam: 'lacking [proper] rule', acc. sg. masc., predicate; simply joined with the following word, final -m unaffected before the vowel); a-sṛṣṭa — not given, not distributed (from sṛj; first member; a-sṛṣṭa+annam→asṛṣṭānnam, a+a→ā); anna — food (a-sṛṣṭa-annam: 'without the giving-out of food', acc. sg. masc., predicate)
glossary.मन्त्रहीनमदक्षिणम्: mantra-hīnam a-dakṣiṇam — mantra — a Vedic mantra, sacred formula (first member); hīna — lacking, devoid of (mantra-hīnam: 'lacking [the proper] mantras', acc. sg. masc., predicate; simply joined with the following word, final -m unaffected before the vowel); a-dakṣiṇa — without [the priestly] fee (from dakṣiṇā, 'a fee to a priest') (a-dakṣiṇam: acc. sg. masc., predicate)
glossary.श्रद्धाविरहितं: śraddhā-virahitam — śraddhā — faith (first member); virahita — devoid of, lacking (past participle of vi-rah; śraddhā-virahitam: 'devoid of faith', acc. sg. masc., predicate)
glossary.तामसं: tāmasam — tāmasa — tamas-natured, belonging to tamas (acc. sg. masc., predicate)
glossary.परिचक्षते: paricakṣate — pari-cakṣ — to call, declare, describe (paricakṣate: present middle 3rd pl., 'they call')
glossary.देवद्विजगुरुप्राज्ञपूजनं: deva-dvija-guru-prājña-pūjanam — deva — a god (first member); dvija — twice-born, a brahmin (second member); guru — a teacher, an elder (third member); prājña — the wise, a sage (fourth member); pūjana — worship, reverence, honoring (deva-dvija-guru-prājña-pūjanam: 'reverence for gods, brahmins, teachers, and the wise', nom. sg. neut., list item)
glossary.शौचमार्जवम्: śaucam ārjavam — śauca — purity, cleanliness (nom. sg. neut., list item; simply joined with ārjavam, final -m unaffected before the vowel); ārjava — uprightness, straightforwardness (nom. sg. neut., list item)
glossary.ब्रह्मचर्यमहिंसा: brahmacaryam ahiṃsā — brahmacarya — celibacy, sexual restraint (lit. 'conduct proper to Vedic study'; nom. sg. neut., list item; simply joined with ahiṃsā, final -m unaffected before the vowel); a-hiṃsā — non-violence, non-injury (nom. sg. fem., list item)
glossary.शारीरं: śārīram — śārīra — bodily, of the body (adj. from śarīra; nom. sg. neut., predicate agreeing with tapas)
glossary.तप: tapaḥ — tapas — austerity (nom. sg. neut., subject; its own visarga simply drops before the following vowel u- of ucyate, hiatus retained — an accepted epic-verse option, already noted at 16.1's svādhyāyas tapa ārjavam)
glossary.उच्यते: ucyate — vac — to speak, say (ucyate: present passive 3rd sg., 'is called')
glossary.अनुद्वेगकरं: an-udvega-karam — an-udvega — not distressing, causing no agitation (first member; a+u→an- before the vowel); kara — making, causing (an-udvega-karam: 'not causing distress', nom. sg. neut., adj. agreeing with vākyam)
glossary.वाक्यं: vākyam — vākya — speech, an utterance (nom. sg. neut., list item)
glossary.सत्यं: satyam — satya — true, truthful (nom. sg. neut., adj. agreeing with vākyam)
glossary.प्रियहितं: priya-hitam — priya — pleasant, agreeable (first member); hita — beneficial, wholesome (priya-hitam: 'pleasant and beneficial', nom. sg. neut., adj. agreeing with vākyam)
glossary.स्वाध्यायाभ्यसनं: svādhyāya-abhyasanam — svādhyāya — study, recitation of one's own [portion of the] Veda (first member; svādhyāya+abhyasanam→svādhyāyābhyasanam, a+a→ā); abhyasana — repeated practice, exercise, habituation (svādhyāya-abhyasanam: 'the regular practice of [Vedic] recitation', nom. sg. neut., list item)

about: Chapter 17, Śraddhātrayavibhāgayoga, the Yoga of the Threefold Division of Faith, opens with a question Arjuna carries over from the last chapter's teaching that scripture must be the standard for action: what of those who ignore scriptural injunction yet still sacrifice with real faith? Kṛṣṇa answers that faith itself is threefold, born of each person's own nature as sattva-, rajas-, or tamas-natured — and that a person, in the end, is what his faith is. He then traces this threefold pattern through one worldly domain after another: the gods, yakṣas, or ghosts each type of person worships; the food each finds appetizing, from the wholesome and nourishing to the bitter and overspiced to the stale and unclean; the sacrifice offered selflessly and by the rule, or for show, or without faith or form; the austerity of body, speech, and mind, practiced with detachment, for recognition, or out of delusion and malice; and the gift given to a worthy recipient without thought of return, or reluctantly for advantage, or with contempt at the wrong time and place. The chapter then turns to its most demanding teaching: the syllables Oṃ, Tat, and Sat are together the threefold name of brahman, by which the whole Vedic order of brahmins, scriptures, and rites was anciently established — Oṃ uttered at the start of every rite, Tat naming the renunciation of a rite's fruit, and Sat naming both existence itself and whatever is good, praiseworthy, or steadfastly pursued. The chapter closes by naming the opposite of all this: whatever is offered, given, or done without faith is asat, without worth, and avails nothing, neither in this world nor the next — faith, and not mere form, is what finally makes an act real.
